author: kbwestfall
body:
This is a significant refactor of the calibration naming approach.  The primary changes are:

 - Default output directory changed from `Masters` to `Calibrations`.
 - Default names now remove the `Master` prefix; e.g., `MasterArc` is now `Arc`.
 - The calibration groups are now included explicitly in the file name.  So arcs with calibration groups = `1,2` will have an output file name like, e.g., `Arc_A_1-2_DET01.fits`.  The only exception to this use of a dash-separated list of integers is the use of all; e.g., `Arc_A_all_DET01.fits`.
 - Previous code used to generate the calibration frame naming has been deprecated in favor of a class hierarchy.  See the new class `pypeit.calibframe.CalibFrame`, which is propagated to all of the files written to the `Calibrations` directory.  This includes classes that previously only subclassed from `DataContainer` (e.g., `EdgeTraceSet`), but also many classes that subclassed from `PypeItImage`, which led to the new class `PypeItCalibrationImage`.
 - This refactor allowed me to clean-up (in my opinion) a lot of hacks in the `DataContainer` class that were used only in subclasses.
 - Changed how the `.calib` file is generated; see changes to `Calibrations`, `PypeItMetaData`, and `PypeItSetup`, and `pypeit_setup`.
 - The names of all the processed calibration frames are now included in the individual headers of the `spec2d` file.  This is generally useful, but it also met the needs of afterburn scripts that needed these file names (e.g., `datacube.py`).
 - Includes a significant update to quick-look.  The `ql_multislit.py` script has been deprecated, but some functionality has not yet been recovered.

For other changes, see `CHANGES.rst`.

Tests pass.  Dev-suite run starting soon.

author: bluss
body:
Implement

* 8x8 sgemm kernel for AArch64 using NEON instructions
* 8x4 dgemm kernel for AArch64 using NEON instructions

**Benchmarks (single thread)**

Using benches/benchloop.py in the repository.
on Apple Silicon M1 (MacBookAir10,1 3.2 GHz) 

* sgemm 96.4 gflop/s at M,N,K = 1024
* dgemm 45.8 gflop/s at M,N,K = 1024

Not revolutionary, comparable (for sgemm) with openblas. (Apple Accelerate uses other proprietary extensions which are miles ahead.)

AArch64 NEON has 32 registers, each 128-bit, corresponding being able to store 128 x f32 or 64 x f64. To keep the whole kernel in memory, the upper limit of kernel size would be somewhere below 16x8 for f32.
Further kernel size and NC, KC, MC tweaks can give further benefits here (less significant compared to the already won performance), this PR is a start.

author: kspieks
body: This PR cleans up the notebooks for producing the splits for the paper. Just some minor reorganization. It also updates the kmeans splits for RDB7. Although different random seeds are passed to the kmeans splitter, for this specific dataset and number of clusters, I noticed that the validation and testing sets often had a lot of overlap between the different random seeds, which is somewhat expected since nothing is explicitly enforcing them to be mutually exclusive. Previously, I was using different random seeds and then checking the first index of each train, val, and test set to visually inspect if the first cluster assignment was the same between different random seeds. This is why I ended up with seeds in range (0, 15, 3) rather than just range(5) to. But obviously this isn’t rigorous enough because even if the 1st cluster is different, the subsequent clusters could still be very similar. Here I directly assign clusters to different folds to ensure no overlap. This issue is much less prevalent for the 100 clusters we create for QM9 so this PR only changes RDB7. I'll make a PR to update the values in the table soon.

body:
### Contribution description

This adds the following modules

- `bus_stats`: Common infrastructure to collect bus usage statistics
- `bus_stats_spi`: SPI hooks to collect usage stats of SPI attached endpoints
    - Via linker magic wrappers are added on top of `spi_acquire()`, `spi_release()`, `spi_transfer_bytes()`, ... to allow collection of statistics
    - Endpoints can be registered for monitoring by adding XFA entries
- `bus_stats_i2c`: Same as `bus_stats_spi`, but for I2C
- `shell_cmd_bus_stats`: Shell command to print / clear bus statistics

The documentation provided contains details on usage, terminology, and metrics.

### Testing procedure

A test application was provided in `tests/sys_bus_stats` that adds monitoring for BME680 and/or BMx280 sensors connected via either SPI or I2C. Additional XFA entries could be easily added to monitor communication more I2C or SPI attached devices.

author: italypaleale
body:
Adds support for Azure AD authentication in the `state.sqlserver` component.

Fixes #2726

1. First, the library we used is now deprecated and replaced by an official, Microsoft-maintained fork: https://github.com/microsoft/go-mssqldb - updated to use that library
2. Second, although the library did already support Azure AD auth (by importing a separate package), it did in a way that was not compatible with the shared Azure auth library all other components use.
   - It's now possible to authenticate with Azure AD by setting `useAzureAD: true` in the metadata.
   - The other Azure AD-related options are required as usual (like "azureClientID", etc)
   - A `connectionString` is still required to include the URL of the database, the DB name, and any connection option. If it contains credentials, they are ignored
3. This required doing some refactoring on the metadata parsing and struct
4. Also added the metadata.yaml 

Note: I confirmed tests pass locally, but I can't easily add them to the certification tests because it appears I may need to create a separate Azure SQL instance to use Azure AD. I can look into doing that in a subsequent PR

author: ships
body:
This integration test suite can be used to ensure that meaningful API contract assumptions are true in the Crossref API. We have noticed discrepancies bewteen reality and the documented swagger files, so with this suite, we can ensure that the responses in actuality are unmarshalable from the JSON to our typescript types.

Currently this test suite only test the `/works` endpoints, and not totally covering all fields in the response. But if there are issues with consumers of this library getting unexpected `undefined` values at runtime, it could be because the generated types do NOT correctly map to the JSON responses, which we can test-drive out by adding constraints to this library. We will therefore also catch regressions in important behavior in the crossref api.

author: tshortli
body:
Cherry pick of https://github.com/apple/swift/pull/65557

Implement a new `-unavailable-decl-optimization` mode that replaces the bodies of unavailable functions with calls to a standard library function that invokes `fatalError`. Unlike `-unavailable-decl-optimization=complete`, this compilation mode is designed to improve the code size of unavailable code while also preserving ABI compatibility. This is important since there are existing compiled binaries that link the symbols for unavailable functions even though those symbols should be provably unreachable.

This optimization is implemented in SILGen by inserting a call to a new standard library function `_diagnoseUnavailableCodeReached()` in the prologue of each unavailable function. The existing dead code elimination optimization pass then determines that the remainder of the function body is unreachable and removes all other code, leaving the body of the function as a single call to a no-return function.

There are several follow up changes that can be made to maximize the effectiveness of this optimization:
- Some functions that could benefit from this optimization are generated during IRGen, like value witnesses functions. The same technique will need to be reproduced for IRGen to reduce code size further.
- The generated machine code for the stubbed functions is not optimal. It currently includes stack pointer management before calling `_diagnoseUnavailableCodeReached()` and sometimes also includes a `brk` instruction after the call. Some work to reduce the machine code for these stubs down to the minimal necessary instructions (probably just a single branch?) may be warranted.

Resolves rdar://107388493

author: obliviousharmony
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing to Gutenberg! Please follow the Gutenberg Contributing Guidelines:
https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/blob/trunk/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## What?
By default all `wp-env run` commands are ran from `/var/www/html`. This means that any relative paths used in a command are relative to this directory. This PR adds a new `--env-cwd` option that changes the working directory for `wp-env run`.

## Why?
In adding support for running PHPUnit tests to our repository, I noticed that running `wp-env run tests-wordpress /var/www/html/wp-content/plugins/woocommerce/vendor/bin/phpunit` in a script and adding a path to a test file does not work. It expects the relative path to be relative to `/var/www/html` instead of the `phpunit.xml` file I use.

As for the name `--env-cwd`, it's important to note that any options registered by `npm` or `wp-env` are consumed by their respective tools instead of being passed on. `--cwd` seems likely to have been used by some tool, so, we should try and avoid conflict.

I've marked this as a breaking change in case someone is using `--env-cwd` in their `wp-env run` commands. Since it's going to consume it there's the possibility it will break for someone.

## How?
We're using the `-w` option provided by `docker-compose run` to change the working directory of the command. This avoids any messiness with trying to `cd`.

## Testing Instructions
1. `npm run env -- run tests-wordpress pwd` should echo `/var/www/html`.
2. `npm run env -- run tests-wordpress --env-cwd=/var  pwd` should echo `/var`.

body:
To mitigate issue #1360.

New error message:

> Incompatible type. The item you are trying to put into a table has a type that is not compatible with the table.

`Union` fails here:
https://github.com/microsoft/Power-Fx/blob/5b890ffe6bd07eff9a7671d01ca100316fcc3c2a/src/libraries/Microsoft.PowerFx.Core/Types/DType.cs#L2813

Then PFx tries to show which column has failed. The problem is that Union fails for a particular reason, but we use a different method to find the problematic column. PFx can accept Polymorphic/Record types. For some reason that I couldn't identify PA Client can't. This will result in `Owner:{e}` and PFx handling this scenario at
https://github.com/microsoft/Power-Fx/blob/5b890ffe6bd07eff9a7671d01ca100316fcc3c2a/src/libraries/Microsoft.PowerFx.Core/Functions/TexlFunction.cs#L888

author: sfc-gh-mrui
body:
SNOW-796952 Add option to disable pre- and post-action validation for session sharing.

The option name is `FORCE_SKIP_PRE_POST_ACTION_CHECK_FOR_SHARED_SESSION`. The default is false.

`preactions` and `postactions` may affect the session level setting, so connection sharing
may be enabled only when the queries in `preactions` and `postactions` are in a white list.
`FORCE_SKIP_PRE_POST_ACTION_CHECK_FOR_SHARED_SESSION` is introduced if users are sure that
the queries in `preactions` and `postactions` don't affect others.

### Changes proposed in this Pull Request:

<!-- Describe the changes made to this Pull Request, and the reason for such changes. -->

Some repository setup and scaffolding a JS/SCSS build workflow. Most setup details match other Newspack repositories. Some specifics for this theme:

- I modified `functions.php` to include class modules like we do in our plugins—this should make it easier to organize PHP functionality into separate files and keep the `functions.php` file from getting too big.
- I put all JS and SCSS files into a `src` folder. Let me know if this structure makes sense:
  - `js/editor` contains a single `index.js` entrypoint which can include all editor-specific JS for the theme. This gets outputted to `dist/editor.js`.
  - `js/front-end` can include any number of entrypoint files. Any `*.js` files directly inside this folder will be compiled separately to `dist` and retain their name. JS files in subfolders won't be compiled, that way you can include other JS files if needed.
  - `js/shared` can contain JS modules that should be shared by editor and front-end JS, to avoid code duplication.
  - `scss` contains the single `style.scss` entrypoint file that will be compiled down to the root `style.css` file. Hint: if you need to include styles in the editor too, you can `import '../scss/<filename>.scss` from a JS file within the `js/editor` folder to compile the styles to `dist/editor.css`.
